data.label: Monitor customer accounts
data.description: Trigger the workflow by continuously monitoring existing customer accounts for churn-risk signals.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic trigger/monitoring step. It can be implemented as a scheduled job, event listener, or polling rule without AI. No uncertainty, prediction, or language understanding is required.
conditions: run on schedule or on account-update event
select active customer accounts only
data.errorHandling: If the scheduler/webhook fails, retry with exponential backoff. If the job is delayed, run a catch-up scan and deduplicate accounts by account_id + window_start. Emit an ops alert after repeated failures.

data.label: Collect churn signals
data.description: Gather usage trends for the last 30 days, negative-sentiment support tickets, and late or failed invoice payment data for each account.
data.rationale: This step is mainly data retrieval from existing systems and can be handled with deterministic API/DB lookups. It does not require ML or language generation; the workflow just gathers structured signals.
conditions: account is active
usage window covers the last 30 days
retrieve latest support and billing records
data.errorHandling: If one source is unavailable, retry the failed API call up to 3 times. If a source still fails, mark the signal as null with source_status='degraded' and continue scoring using available signals. Do not drop the account; log partial retrieval for audit.

data.label: Assess usage decline
data.description: Determine whether product usage has dropped over the last 30 days.
data.rationale: This can be computed deterministically by comparing usage metrics across a 30-day window. A rule-based percentage drop calculation is sufficient, so no ML is needed.
conditions: usage records available for current and prior 30-day windows
calculate percentage drop = (prior_30d - current_30d) / prior_30d
data.errorHandling: Validate usage inputs before calculation. If prior_30d is zero or missing, set usage_decline to false and usage_drop_pct to null. If input parsing fails, log validation error and continue with a conservative default of no decline.

data.label: Check support sentiment
data.description: Identify support tickets tagged with negative sentiment for the account.
data.rationale: At L0, this is only possible if tickets are already manually tagged. The description implies identifying negative-sentiment tickets, which usually requires NLP/NLU classification over ticket text or metadata. That is a language-understanding task, so L2 is appropriate.
conditions: support tickets exist for the account
classify or filter tickets tagged negative-sentiment
prefer existing tag if present; otherwise infer sentiment from text
data.errorHandling: If ticket text is unavailable, fall back to metadata tags only. If NLP classification fails, mark sentiment as unknown and continue. Use a confidence threshold; below threshold, do not mark as negative unless a manual tag exists.

data.label: Check payment status
data.description: Identify late or failed invoice payments associated with the account.
data.rationale: Payment status is structured operational data. This is a straightforward rule/lookup check against billing records, so L0 is sufficient.
conditions: invoice status in late, failed, unpaid, past_due
consider only invoices within the last billing cycle unless otherwise configured
data.errorHandling: If billing lookup fails, retry the API call. If still unavailable, mark payment_status as unknown and continue scoring. Do not assume late payment without evidence.

data.label: Score churn risk
data.description: Combine the churn signals and assign each account a churn-risk score from 0 to 100.
data.rationale: L0 can combine signals with fixed weights, but the requirement to assign a risk score from 0 to 100 suggests a learned or calibrated scoring model is likely intended. If this is a trained churn model, it fits L1 supervised ML. No language generation is needed.
conditions: ingest usage_decline, support_negative_sentiment, payment_late_or_failed
normalize score to 0-100
apply calibrated model or weighted rules
data.errorHandling: If the model is unavailable, fall back to a deterministic weighted rule score. If one or more signals are missing, score using available features and include missing_signal_flags in the output. Clamp final score to 0-100.

data.label: Route by risk score
data.description: Branch the workflow based on whether the score is above 75, between 40 and 75, or below 40.
data.rationale: Pure threshold-based branching. This is standard deterministic if/then/else logic with no AI requirement.
conditions: score is an integer or float between 0 and 100
data.errorHandling: If score is missing or invalid, route to the error handling path by defaulting to passive monitoring and logging a scoring exception for review.

data.label: Notify CSM
data.description: Immediately notify the assigned Customer Success Manager for high-risk accounts.
data.rationale: Notification routing is deterministic automation: pick the assigned CSM and send an alert through a messaging or CRM integration. No AI is required.
conditions: score > 75
assigned CSM must exist
data.errorHandling: If the CSM profile cannot be found, route to a team inbox or CSM manager fallback. Retry notification delivery twice. If delivery still fails, log a failed-notification event and continue to email drafting.

data.label: Draft retention email
data.description: Create a personalized retention outreach email for the high-risk account.
data.rationale: This requires generating personalized natural-language content. A single LLM call can draft the email based on account context without needing external tools, so L3 fits.
conditions: score > 75
include account context, recent churn signals, and CSM tone guidance
data.errorHandling: If the LLM call fails, retry with a reduced prompt. If generation still fails, create a minimal template email with placeholders and mark it for manual review. Avoid hallucinating account-specific facts not present in the input.

data.label: Queue CSM review
data.description: Add medium-risk accounts to a weekly Customer Success Manager review queue.
data.rationale: This is deterministic queue insertion based on a score range. No AI or language processing is required.
conditions: queue for the next weekly CSM review cycle
data.errorHandling: If queue insertion fails, retry once and then write to a durable dead-letter table for later reprocessing. Ensure the account is not duplicated by enforcing idempotency on account_id + review_week.

data.label: Continue passive monitoring
data.description: Keep low-risk accounts under passive monitoring without additional intervention.
data.rationale: This is a simple deterministic pass-through state. It does not involve prediction, language understanding, or tool orchestration beyond maintaining the existing monitoring rule.
conditions: score < 40
data.errorHandling: If passive monitoring state update fails, retry and then log the failure for later reconciliation. Do not escalate low-risk accounts unless a scoring or data integrity error occurs.

data.label: Log scoring decision
data.description: Record each account's churn-risk score and the input signals used for audit purposes.
data.rationale: Audit logging is deterministic data persistence. It records already-computed values and inputs for traceability, so L0 is sufficient.
conditions: always log after scoring and downstream action
include account_id, score, input signals, branch taken, timestamp, and model/version metadata
data.errorHandling: If audit write fails, retry with backoff and then append to a durable outbox table. Never block customer actions solely because audit logging is unavailable; reconcile later with the outbox.

data.condition: one or more sources temporarily unavailable
data.label: retry failed source fetch

data.condition: model unavailable or feature validation failed
data.label: retry scoring

message: This workflow uses deterministic data collection and rule evaluation in parallel, then scores churn risk using a calibrated ML model or weighted fallback. Threshold routing sends high-risk accounts to immediate CSM notification and LLM-based email drafting, medium-risk accounts to a weekly review queue, and low-risk accounts to passive monitoring. Every path ends in audit logging with full input-signal traceability, and each critical step includes retry, fallback, and error logging behavior.

workflow.workflowBrief: Monitor existing customer accounts for churn-risk signals: drop in product usage over the last 30 days, support tickets tagged negative-sentiment, and late or failed invoice payments. Score each account's churn risk from 0 to 100. For scores above 75, immediately notify the assigned Customer Success Manager and draft a personalized retention outreach email. For scores between 40 and 75, add the account to a weekly CSM review queue. For scores below 40, continue passive monitoring. Log every scoring decision with the input signals for audit.
